emulate_text: Note that "outside" doesn't have to mean the nation state, though at first, when doing this research, that's where it seemed to have to go. The basic need here is for a competent level of authority that is not reviewing its own actions. That could mean another community, a federation of communities, professionals, autonomous regional institutions, courts, regulatory agencies, emergency services, etc. The key is that it's not the same people! An important correction that came from the Zapatistas: it's ok for that authority to be in a regional institution as long as it's autonomous, and doesn't combine its powers with the other institutions. But when it tried to push power upwards, they pushed it back down again. And no, it still can't decide that individual people don't have certain non-waivable rights.
v26: 'Outside' doesn't always mean the nation-state. [My research](https://innerself.185-233-106-15.sslip.io/blog/commune-article-research/) initially leaned too far that way. What's really needed is that there be a competent layer that isn't reviewing its own conduct. That can be another community, a federation, a professional, an autonomous regional institution, a court, a regulatory agency, an emergency service. Just not whoever's being reviewed! The Zapatistas are an important correction here: autonomous institutions can review local power without becoming the state, and when power crept up in their own system, they pushed it back down. But autonomy doesn't mean that anyone can erase non-waivable individual rights, or that outside jurisdiction disappears.
